_readme: Technical Product Marketing, Version 1.6: the rebuilt case study through 01 Hero, 02 Foundation, 03 the transitional statement, 04 Website, 05 Technical documentation, 06 the flagship animation campaign and 07 the conclusion, then Contact (Selected Writing, added in V1.3, was taken out in V1.4; V1.5 gave the hero the Narrative Engine and the signal field and made the conclusion the dark closing movement into Contact; V1.6 replaced the engine and the field with the isometric system and gave the hero its section label). Copy is John's approved wording from the V1 concept, the V1.1, V1.2, V1.3, V1.4, V1.5 and V1.6 briefs and the V1.2 delta brief (October 12 to 14, 2026); `accent` names the one phrase of a headline set in the accent color and `em` the one phrase of a paragraph set a little heavier (V1.3: a handful of each across the page, never both on one phrase); the chapter notes under the documentation walkthrough are drafted from the brief's confirmed facts and are open to John's edits. The foundation library lists twelve named documents in the brief's order, with display numbers 00 to 11 (not their Linear numbers); no document body is read, quoted or published. Full Site Iteration V1 (October 2026): the documentation's goal, contribution and overview note say outdated rather than fragmented, scattered or connected; the interactive architecture note keeps John's part only (Bob van der Meer stays credited in the documentation's credits); the conclusion reaches past the three featured examples to the whole public-facing system.

hero._hero: The section label, then the headline and paragraph on the left, the isometric system on the right (V1.6, replacing the V1.5 Narrative Engine and its signal field), the seven scope terms in one centered line beneath them (V1.4); no media. The headline never changes; `break` is the phrase its first line ends with, so it always sets in two lines, sized to its column.
hero.label: 02 / Technical Product Marketing
hero.headline: Building the system behind the message.
hero.copy: I built the strategic foundation that turned Bolt Liquidity’s technical complexity into a clear market narrative, then carried it across documentation, web experiences, articles, and campaigns.
hero._system: The hero's isometric system (V1.6, replacing the V1.5 Narrative Engine and its signal field): research and inputs on the left, the shared product language at the center as an architectural foundation, the public-facing expressions on the right. Its geometry is src/lib/tpm-iso.ts. `labels` are the few words shown only while the system is engaged (pointer over it, a tap, or its control), keyed by component; `description` is what assistive technology reads for the drawing; `toggle` is the control that shows and hides the labels for keyboards and screen readers.

system.description: Stakeholder interviews, product research and foundational marketing documents feed a shared product language, built at the center as an architectural foundation, which carries through to the website, the technical documentation, and campaigns and content.

foundation._headline: Always two lines, broken where the brief breaks it.
headline: Before the message
comes the foundation.
foundation._copy: Two paragraphs (the companion pass in the Events V1.1 brief): the first sentence stands alone, with room beneath it; `em` is in the first.
copy: Before a product can be explained externally, it needs a shared internal language.

For Bolt Liquidity, I built that language from stakeholder interviews and product research, shaping the positioning, claims, proof points, and narrative architecture behind every public-facing expression.
foundation._documents: In the brief's order, from internal input through market understanding, strategic definition, governance and expression. Each document has its own muted accent (its strip and its faded icon) and its own icon; no two neighbors share a hue family. The interview count is not published.
foundation._depth: Unlabeled, neutral covers after the last named document: no number, title, subline or icon, only the suggestion that the library runs deeper.
foundation._stack: Mobile Optimization V1: on phones (below 48rem) one composed stack of these documents (by number, from the back of the stack to the front: each card behind shows its number and title, the front card shows whole) stands in for the whole library, with `line` beneath it; the full library stays in the page for assistive technology. No control opens the rest.

stack.line: The work grew into a multi-document marketing foundation.

statement.copy: Once the product language is clear, it guides every expression that follows: the website, technical documentation, articles, campaigns, and content that bring the product to market.
statement._highlight: The page's one animated highlight (V1.3): once the statement has been revealed, a translucent teal sweeps behind this clause, the one that says how the shared language guides every public-facing expression.
statement.highlight: it guides every expression that follows

website.title: Website
website._meta: Label and value pairs, in order. **Text** marks a name set in bold.

meta.label: Goal
value: Translate the company’s new positioning into a credible, conversion-focused website.

meta.label: Services
value: Web strategy, information architecture, copywriting, UX direction, and conversion design.

meta.label: Credits
value: Visual design and development: **Bob van der Meer**.

website._contribution: Centered beneath the metadata. Bob's name is in the credits and is not repeated here.
website.contribution: I mapped the experience from the opening section to the final CTA, wrote the complete website narrative, shaped its scroll behavior and interactions, and defined the partnership journey and form flow. Working closely with design, I guided each revision through a complete rebuild and launch in two weeks.
website.em: a complete rebuild and launch in two weeks
website._live: The live site, beside the display and outside it (V1.3). It opens in a new tab, and assistive technology hears where it goes (ExternalLink).

documentation.title: Technical documentation

meta.label: Goal
value: Replace outdated documentation with a clear, structured system for technical audiences while controlling what product information could be made public.

meta.label: Services
value: Documentation strategy, information architecture, technical writing, content governance, and MDX implementation.

meta.label: Credits
value: Visual design and interactive implementation: **Bob van der Meer**.

documentation._contribution: Centered beneath the metadata. Bob's name is in the credits and is not repeated here.
documentation.contribution: I rebuilt the documentation from the ground up, moving it from an outdated GitBook into a purpose-built Mintlify documentation system. I owned the architecture, technical writing, cross-references, calls to action, MDX build, and GitHub publishing, working across engineering, growth, and design to make complex product information useful, accurate, and appropriate for public release.
documentation.em: useful, accurate, and appropriate for public release
documentation._chapters: The three proof points of the edited walkthrough, introduced as selected views from a broader documentation system, with where each begins in it (seconds, at the middle of the cross-fade into it). The notes are drafted from the brief's confirmed facts.
documentation.chaptersLabel: Selected views from a broader documentation system

chapters.title: Documentation overview
chapters.note: One branded Mintlify system in place of outdated GitBook documentation, organized from product understanding to implementation.

chapters.title: Interactive architecture
chapters.note: I developed the early diagram with engineering, validated it with the liquidity team, refined its structure, filtered out internal-only information, briefed design, and wrote every pop-up explanation.

chapters.title: Developer SDK
chapters.note: The existing SDK code was preserved while the surrounding structure, explanations, cross-references, navigation, and presentation were rebuilt.

campaign._title: The chapter's headline, in place of a name: 06 Flagship animation campaign.
campaign.title: One minute to make the product clear.

meta.label: Goal
value: Create a flagship product explanation that could anchor the brand’s X profile, build awareness across the target ecosystem, and direct interest toward the website and technical documentation.

meta.label: Services
value: Campaign concept, narrative strategy, storyboarding, voiceover direction, creative direction, and distribution strategy.

meta.label: Credits
value: Animation and visual production: **Bob van der Meer**.

campaign._contribution: Centered beneath the metadata. Bob's name is in the credits and is not repeated here.
campaign.contribution: I conceived the campaign, mapped the one-minute narrative from first frame to final CTA, built the storyboard, and recorded reference voiceover tracks that guided the finished AI-generated narration. I worked closely with design through each revision, then coordinated amplification across partners, ecosystem accounts, and creators.
campaign.em: mapped the one-minute narrative from first frame to final CTA
campaign._results: The launch post's first 48 hours. The 84 percent is a share of impressions (reach beyond the followers), never of engagements. **Text** is set in bold; spoken is what a screen reader says in place of a value with a symbol it would read aloud.

results.label: First 48 hours after launch
supporting: Recognized and amplified by **key ecosystem foundation accounts**

ecosystem._note: V1.3, polished in V1.4 (October 2026): after the campaign's results and before the conclusion (TpmEcosystem.astro). John's approved copy, word for word; **text** is set in bold. accent is the headline's phrase in the accent color. Centered throughout: the narrative, then a divider, then the volume beside the integrations. The logos name the aggregators, so the copy does not. The downstream reach is never counted.
ecosystem.headline: Product clarity carried into the market.
ecosystem.copy: The same product fluency behind the positioning, website, documentation, and campaign also supported ecosystem growth. I helped translate Bolt's value and architecture into **partner conversations and direct integrations**. The work also created **downstream integration paths** as the protocol grew from zero to **more than $300 million in processed volume**.

conclusion._conclusion: 07 The closing frame (V1.3, renumbered when Selected Writing left in V1.4; since V1.5 a full screen on the dark closing ground that turns into the Contact green): a synthesis, not a summary. Only the way on to the next case study follows the copy, as one linked sentence (V1.4) that names it; `next` is that case study's id, which must be the next in the collection's order. No metrics, services, credits or roles.
conclusion.headline: One foundation. Every expression aligned.
conclusion.copy: The work began with a shared product language and carried across the full public-facing system, from the website and technical documentation to campaigns, articles, content, and every expression built from the same strategic foundation.
conclusion.nextLine: Next, see how I bring events and multimedia production from concept through execution.
